analysis: The method begins with a precondition check (checkState) that throws IllegalStateException if inputStreamEnded is true. Then it computes offset and size from inputBuffer.data if not null and has remaining. If end-of-stream, it sets inputStreamEnded and flags. Then it calls mediaCodec.queueInputBuffer, which may throw MediaCodec.CodecException (a runtime exception) or IllegalStateException if the codec is in an invalid state. After the call, it sets inputBufferIndex to C.INDEX_UNSET and inputBuffer.data to null. If an exception is thrown by mediaCodec.queueInputBuffer, the subsequent cleanup statements are skipped, leaving the object in an inconsistent state: inputStreamEnded may have been set even though the buffer was not successfully queued, inputBufferIndex remains set to a value that may no longer be valid, and inputBuffer.data is not nulled. Therefore, it is necessary to catch these runtime exceptions around the call and revert the state changes before propagating the exception.
